newsitem.title: LATVIA: BUSINESS NEWSPAPERS LAUNCH STOCK INDEX.
newsitem.headline: BUSINESS NEWSPAPERS LAUNCH STOCK INDEX.

text.p: The three biggest Baltic business newspapers launched their joint stock index Baltic30 on Tuesday, tracking the 10 top stocks from Riga, Tallinn and Vilnius, the Dienas bizness said.
The three newspapers are 49 to 51 percent owned by the Swedish Dagens Industri AB, controlled by the Bonnier Business Press.
"The basic idea with the index is to have a higher profile for the Baltic countries in the international business news market," Juris Paiders, editor-in-chief of Diena bizness, told Reuters.
"Each Baltic country on its own would never make it but jointly we are a market of eight million people and have potential to be on par with Sweden or Finland in 20 years time," he added.
Editors of the three papers, Aeripaev, Verslo Zinios and Dienas bizness are meeting in Tallinn Wednesday to dicuss ways of disseminating the index.
"I would expect the index to appear in the Swedish Dagens Industri, which is only a matter of time," Paider said. "Other possibilities will also be dicussed."
The newspapers also plan to launch the Baltic30 investment fund this autumn, to be coordinated by the Estonian Aeripaev, which earlier this year began a fund linked to its bourse index.
"We want B30 to have not only an academic but also a business value," Paiders said.
